measurement: ISOLATED and STILL PRESENT ON CURRENT MASTER. Necessary condition: an in-flight SSE stream idle in rd.next() when SIGTERM lands (~25%: 5/20 arms on b10533, 2/6 on a 074f1f3 build of 2026-11-26). Duration governed by sse_ping_interval, proved by intervention: default 30 -> 30.43/30.32/30.32/30.29/30.27 s and 31.46/31.48 s on master; --sse-ping-interval 5 -> 6.34/6.35/5.38 s. Never an intermediate value. Inside a caught stall all 9 surviving threads sit in futex_wait_queue, the listener thread is gone, the client socket stays ESTAB, and the log gap between 'cleaning up before exit' and 'cancel task' is exactly 30.0034 s, then exit in 164 ms.
notes: CAUSE: clean_up() runs session_manager_stop(); ctx_http.stop(); ctx_server.terminate() -- the cancel that would release the waiting SSE handler is issued AFTER the wait it would release, and nothing in the handler's stop condition observes shutdown, so it waits for the keep-alive ping (sse_ping_interval, 30). *** CORRECTION 2026-11-26: the 2026-11-25 claim that this was ALREADY FIXED UPSTREAM is WITHDRAWN. master's sse_stopping flag is passed ONLY to the /models/sse handler; the completion routes (/completion, /completions, /v1/chat/completions) never consult it. A freshly built 074f1f3 still stalls 2/6 at ~31 s. So upgrading does NOT fix it and the bug IS worth filing. *** RETRACTED en route: 'aged instance', 'newer-build regression', 'deterministic in n_predict', 'per-slot context boundary', 'SIGTERM fails to cancel generation', and 'already fixed upstream'. Mitigation TimeoutStopSec=15 remains correct. Unexplained: stall is sse_ping_interval + 0.3-1.3 s (probably the 1 s HTTP_POLLING_SECONDS granularity); and the 120.26 s reading hit a TimeoutStopSec=120 cap so its true length is unknown and is NOT this 30 s mechanism.

No published llama.cpp result quantifies this; a turingpi.com write-up attributes a 4-thread win to cluster locality without measuring it, and a TVM result on other silicon found little cores HELPING, so it is SoC-specific. notes: tj trip points are 35/74/95/104 C, so 86 C is past the third trip with no clamping -- the governor does NOT protect a sustained run, and fan headroom remains. First attempt was VOID: it used 8 streams and peaked at 80 C, because paper 006 shows 2->8 streams drops module power ~4.5 W, making 8 streams the COLDEST config -- the experiment was run in the setting least likely to show the effect. Also void in that run: 'min GPU clock 0 MHz' was a failed read of a nonexistent sysfs path (/sys/devices/17000000.gpu/devfreq/...); the real path is /sys/class/devfreq/17000000.gpu/cur_freq.
